title: Unknown command exit codes are classified as failures
reasoning: ToolEvent explicitly permits an unknown exit code through None, but every failure predicate uses exit_code != 0. Since None != 0 is true, commands without a recorded result count as failed tests and can create false fix cycles and edits-after-failure metrics even when there is no error output.
reproduction: Call detect_bug_fix_cycles with a Bash test event whose exit_code is None and has_error_output is false. failed_test_runs becomes 1. Append an Edit and another test event to also produce a false test_fix_retest cycle.
recommendation: Centralize failure detection and require a known nonzero exit code or positive error evidence. Preserve unknown outcomes separately.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were supplied for unknown outcomes or incomplete trajectories.
suggestedRegressionTest: Cover zero, nonzero, and unknown exit codes with and without error evidence across run counts, fix cycles, and subsequent-edit metrics.
minimumFixScope: Failure predicates in detect_bug_fix_cycles and behavioral coverage for unknown outcomes.
